Subject: Request: Unwind window & downgrade protections for Helix pilot (approval needed)

Hi team and Sarah —

Quick context: Helix wants a 6-month pilot (4 months usage + optional 2-month evaluation) but procurement pushed for a 30-day unwind (they call it an "exit window") and firm downgrade protections so they can reduce committed capacity after month 2 without penalty. The commercial ask is: a 30-day unwind window + a staged downsell protection (50% commit in month 1-2, 30% month 3-4, then full commit thereafter) and an opt-out clause tied to product regressions.

Why this matters: If we accept the 30-day exit window + generous downgrade thresholds it materially increases our unit economics risk on dedicated capacity for Q3. We can trade that for a higher setup fee and a capped downgrade credit schedule.

What I need: executive approval for the attached ramp/downgrade language (see redwood_ramp_terms_draft.docx) or guidance on acceptable guardrails. If leadership prefers, we can offer a shorter unwind (45–60 days) in exchange for a 20% higher onboarding fee and a minimum-billing floor.

Attachments: helix_sow_v2.pdf (SOW), redwood_ramp_terms_draft.docx (proposed contract language)

Proposed next steps:
- Approve the attached language as-is (fastest to close)
- Or give direction on minimum allowed unwind and downgrade credit cap

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call.

Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference

Kim —

Thanks for the write-up and the docs. Quick thoughts:
- 30-day unwind is tight but may be acceptable if we secure a non-refundable onboarding/setup fee that covers a portion of ramp costs.
- Downgrade schedule should be capped to a single crediting event (not rolling month-to-month) to avoid repeated churn on reserved capacity.
- Opt-out tied to objective SLOs (p95 latency > X ms for 3 consecutive days OR model-quality dropped below agreed prompt set eval threshold) is reasonable. We need legal to draft the exact metrics.

Karthik — can you review the attached language and flag anything we can't accept? If legal is OK, I support the onboarding fee + 30-day unwind + single-event downgrade credit (50% of difference up to N months).

Team —

I reviewed redwood_ramp_terms_draft.docx. High-level legal guidance:
- We can accept a 30-day unwind only if we: (a) make onboarding fee non-refundable to cover initial allocation, and (b) explicitly exclude active reserved GPU allocations from downgrade credit (credits apply to subscription fees, not one-time infra commitments).
- Downgrade credit should be a one-time credit applied to future invoices (not a cash refund). Contract must specify calculation: (Committed units - actual average units over first 60 days) * unit price * cap (max credit = 3 months of difference).
- Opt-out metrics must be concrete and measured by shared telemetry (both parties need read access to the same usage dashboard) — otherwise subject to dispute. Include an audit clause and a 7-day remediation window before opt-out executes.

I redlined the doc and attached suggested language. If sales wants more flexibility on credits (cash refunds), we need an approval from finance (Rishi) since that impacts revenue recognition and cash.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts

Appreciate the summary. My view from finance:
- Approve the 30-day unwind only with the following mandatory commercials: 1) non-refundable onboarding fee equal to 15% of the first-year ARR; 2) downgrade credit must be a one-time invoice credit (no cash refunds); 3) capped maximum credit equal to 3 months of the committed/actual difference; 4) require shared telemetry and a 7-day cure period before opt-out.
- If Sales wants to offer cash refunds instead of credits, we need to set aside a reserves bucket and secure approval from VP Finance (not me) — that slows close and increases revenue risk.

Marissa / Kimberly — please confirm you can offer the onboarding fee and that Sales will accept credit-only downgrade mechanics. If yes, legal (Karthik) should finalize language and we can push for signature.
